edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults with hypertension, diabetes, or CKD
edges.mechanism: ACE inhibition reduces efferent arteriolar tone and proteinuric stress, lowering intraglomerular pressure. That can preserve kidney function long term even though creatinine may bump transiently when treatment starts.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Yang meta analysis in Front Med (Lausanne) already points to ace inhibitors tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
